Hazel is built in evenings and weekends, and it is given away because a downloader that charges for the download is a worse downloader. Sites change constantly, and keeping up with them is the work.
If the app saved you an afternoon, anything below puts that time back into it. If it did not, the ways that cost nothing help just as much.
Monthly or one off, cancel whenever. Handled entirely by GitHub.
A one off, no account needed.
The one number people look at before trying an app.
Word of mouth is the whole of this app\'s marketing.
A site that stopped working is a fix nobody else can write.
Every line of it is public, and pull requests are welcome.
No advertisements, nothing measured about what you download, and no feature held back for anyone. Support changes how much time goes into Hazel, not what it will do for you.

Only turn this on if links hang on your network. It works around a broken IPv6 route, and is slower everywhere else.
Give up quickly. Fastest on a good network, but more likely to need a second attempt.
A middle ground between speed and tolerating a poor connection.
Wait longer and retry more. Slowest, but survives a weak network.
The same engine that does the downloading. Works on every site it supports, and updates itself, so it keeps working as sites change.
Lists playlists and channels in one request instead of starting the engine, which is quicker on the sites it knows. Falls back to yt-dlp for everything else, and whenever it cannot read a link.
